title: Choose Unprompted's visual world
question: Re-roll two. The Pairings Sheet is eliminated. Your pin is held. The roll assigned Certificate of Analysis.

options.label: Certificate of Analysis
options.lineage: Laboratory assay reporting: sample IDs, method references, replicate measurements, tolerances, instrument traces, a signed and dated result
options.thesis: Unprompted does not have an opinion. It runs an assay on the machines and publishes the readout, method included.
options.viewport: This week's result sheet: sample ID and method version in the header, brands as measured specimens down the page, each rotation figure carrying its replicate count and spread, deviations flagged in the margin.
options.risk: Clinical worlds can read cold, which fights the brief's demand for heavy animation and visual pleasure.

options.label: Used-Future Crew Terminal
options.lineage: Working starship terminal: green and amber phosphor on curved CRT, stencilled equipment codes, striped hazard plates
options.thesis: You key a query and the glass answers in typed capitals, one line at a time.
options.case: Held at your instruction. Its query-and-answer grammar genuinely fits the name, and phosphor-plus-amber is a real two-role color system rather than a decorative glow. If it wins, I solve the small-screen legibility properly rather than shipping a shrunken CRT.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.lineage: Rail concourse departure board at rush hour: cascading letter flaps, fixed columns, amber delay lamps
options.thesis: A live ranked board where every change arrives as a cascade of clacking characters.
options.case: The strongest card in this hand after the roll. A departures board is already a ranked table that reorders itself on a schedule, which is exactly what a weekly chart is, and the flap cascade answers the heavy-animation requirement with motion that means something instead of decorating.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.lineage: Early one-bit computing: dithered grays, title bars and close boxes, marching-ants selections, 32-pixel icons
options.thesis: Two colors, honest chrome, and a selection border that never stops walking.
options.case: Fuses better than it looks: pure black and white is unbeatable for dense tabular legibility on a phone, and it is inherently screenshot-friendly. Fights the brief's demand for modern, and a two-color world cannot carry rise-and-fall coding without inventing a third.

options.label: Wiener Werkstätte Lattice
options.lineage: Hoffmann metalwork showroom: hammered silver pierced with perfect square holes, strict black-and-white lattices
options.thesis: Every cell a square, every square either pierced open or filled solid.
options.case: The lattice is a genuinely good chassis for a data grid and the filled-cell active state is elegant. But a luxury showroom has nothing to say about measurement, so the world would be decoration bolted to the product rather than an argument about it.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The analytics dashboard every AI-visibility tool ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Dark navy ground, card grid, a line chart hero, one accent gradient, clean sans throughout.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Profound, Peec and Otterly, which is the exact comparison this product exists to escape.
